title: Data residency & region pinning - security review
summary: Redwood (AE+SE) walked through data residency and region-pinning options for NordicBanking, covering EU-only hosting, cross-border processing, sub-processor list, KMS/BYOK options, audit logs and RBAC/SSO controls. Customer requested SOC 2 / ISO docs, architecture diagram for EU-only routing, and a pilot of an EU-only endpoint. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Audit logs, retention, and access controls
action_items: Alex Chen: Send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO attestation, and standard security pack by 2026-11-07
Priya Nair: Provide EU-only architecture diagram and configuration snippets for region pinning by 2026-11-10
Maja Berg: Share list of regulated data types and retention requirements by 2026-11-09
Redwood Ops: Stand up EU-only pilot endpoint and run sample routing test (target week of 2026-11-16)
Erik Svensson: Provide any contract language requirements re: sub-processors by 2026-11-12
next_steps: Schedule SE deep dive to test EU-only routing and VPC options
Share region-pinning example config + IP ranges and subnet info
Draft contract/data processing addendum (DPA) language for review
header: Date: 2026-11-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lars Holm (CISO - NordicBanking), Maja Berg (Head of Platform), Erik Svensson (Legal), Sofia Lind (SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE, and Priya is our SE. we're here to run through data residency and region pinning requirements you flagged.
[00:18] Lars (CISO): Hi Alex, hi Priya. yes, we've got some strict EU-only rules for our retail banking customers. we can't have any customer PII leave eu borders; also need a list of sub-procs and assurances re: cross-border processing.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely. quick overview: Redwood supports hosted EU-only endpoints, Dedicated reserved pools in region, and our Private deployment options if you need private control plane. for hosted we offer region pinning — you can pin requests to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 and we will keep compute and storage in-region.
[00:52] Maja (Head of Platform): when you say storage, do you mean logs, kv cache, and everything? what about backups and snapshots?
[01:04] Priya: yes, by default data at rest for a pinned region stays in-region — that includes model input, logs, and cache snapshots. backups can be configured to stay in-region too. one note: some auxiliary services like analytics or billing are treated as control plane and can be configured to not include PII; we can show where that lives.
[01:25] Sofia (SRE): are any of the control plane services in us or shared across regions? our compliance team wants the control plane out of the EU as well if possible.
[01:36] Alex: good question — our hosted control plane is multi-region but we offer an option: for customers with strict residency we offer Private/Private control plane deployments or Dedicated with regional control plane. that gives you EU-only control plane and no cross-border control plane data. this is more of an enterprise privacy option.
[01:56] Lars: ok — can you provide SOC 2 and ISO certifications? and details on encryption — who owns keys?
[02:06] Alex: yes we'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO documents. on keys we support Redwood-managed KMS, customer-managed KMS, and HSM/BYOK for private deployments. for hosted EU-only you can choose BYOK so keys never leave your KMS.
[02:25] Priya: to add, our encryption at rest uses AES-256; in transit TLS1.2/1.3. when using customer-managed keys, logs and snapshots are encrypted with your key material in the region.
[02:40] Erik (Legal): sub-processors — we need the list and any processors outside the eu that might touch metadata. what's your subprocess list?
[02:50] Priya: our common sub-processors are AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west, and some analytics providers. we can provide a full SCC/sub-processor list and a DPA. note: some telemetry for product improvement is opt-in and we can disable telemetry for EU-only contracts.
[03:12] Maja: about cross-border processing — we can't have routing cause requests to hop to US for model fallback. is there an automatic fallback that would cross borders?
[03:23] Priya: by default fallbacks respect region pinning. we have policy-based routing: latency, cost, and model compatibility, but for customers that require strict residency we can disable cross-region fallback and use region-restricted model variants. there is a small set of model variants that might not be available in a region — we'll list those and propose on-prem or dedicated variants.
[03:50] Lars: how do you prove residency? audit logs?
[03:56] Alex: we provide audit logs with region tags, request traces, and token-level metadata. audit logs are stored in the region when pinned; we can export logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding to your EU SIEM. retention windows are configurable — default 90 days but we can extend.
[04:15] Sofia: who can access logs — internal redwood ops? we need RBAC and SSO integration and proof of least privilege.
[04:24] Priya: we support SAML SSO / enterprise SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. you can restrict access to audit logs to specific roles; access is logged and requires approval for support access. we also support just-in-time support access with customer approval.
[04:45] Erik: is there a support path that doesn't require us to share PII with your support engineers?
[04:52] Alex: yes — for sensitive customers we have a support model where you run targeted runbooks and share redacted logs, or we can set up a private support channel where logs remain in your VPC and we only get scoped view. we'll capture that in the DPA.
[05:10] [00:05:10] Priya: (slightly garbled) also, about KMS: if you use BYOK and an HSM, Redwood cannot decrypt without the key; we don't persist plaintext keys. for Private deployments you can also use on-prem KMS connectors and HSM-backed keys.
[05:30] Lars: do you have any independent pen test or third-party attestations?
[05:36] Alex: yes we have annual pen tests and a summary report; we'll include the pen test summary and any remediation notes in the compliance pack.
[05:47] Maja: what about sub-processors for model hosting — do you use any US-resident model optimizers or inference tooling that might call home?
[05:56] Priya: the runtime is our own, but we do use cloud provider managed GPUs in-region; we don't call home to US services for inference. any telemetry is optional. if you need, we can run an in-region benchmark so you can see that inference happens entirely in eu.
[06:18] Sofia: about logs retention — we need seven years for some datasets. can you escrow logs or provide cold storage?
[06:26] Priya: yes — we can export to your object store in-region and set cold storage policies; export can be encrypted with your keys.
[06:35] [00:06:35] Erik: contractually, we need to ensure sub-processor changes trigger notification and approval for critical sub-processors.
[06:44] Alex: we can add notification windows and high-risk sub-processor approvals in the DPA; standard is 30 days notice but we can discuss.
[06:55] Lars: one more — do you allow data localization at per-tenant level? our business units want separate regions per tenant.
[07:05] Priya: yes, region pinning is tenant-level; you can pin different tenants to different regions. For Dedicated or Private deploys you can also partition capacity per tenant.
[07:22] Maja: technical follow-up: we want an architecture diagram that shows routing, control plane separation, and key flows.
[07:28] Alex: will do.
[07:32] [00:07:32] Priya: quick demo note — region pinning is configured via the accounts API or Console route config; we can show the API payload. also you can set a strict residency policy which disables cross-region fallbacks and external model fetches.
[07:50] Sofia: are subprocessor datacenters all in the eu? some of our auditors ask specifically about personnel access.
[07:58] Priya: we can provide SOC-relevant attestations per sub-processor and scoping of personnel access. for examples, AWS eu-west staff with a eu employment are the usual operators; for cases where staff outside EU might have break glass we can note controls.
[08:16] Lars: what about encryption keys during backups — can we maintain key escrow?
[08:22] Priya: yes BYOK/HSM means you keep key control; we support key rotation APIs. for hosted we integrate with customer KMS in-region via standard KMS integrations and we never transfer plaintext keys.
[08:36] Erik: please confirm legal — we may need SCCs or EU standard contractual clauses and possibly additional contractual safeguards.
[08:44] Alex: we will include the DPA with SCCs. if needed we can also support EU representative clauses.
[08:53] [00:08:53] Maja: any limitations on model variants in-region? eg: some large quantized variants might only be deployed in certain regions due to capacity.
[09:03] Priya: correct — some experimental variants live in a subset of regions. for strict residency we either provide region-compatible variants or Dedicated/Private deployment with the variant deployed in your region. we'll list which variants are region-limited.
[09:22] Sofia: how do you audit that requests stayed in-region? can we get a trace for a request?
[09:28] Priya: yes request trace includes region tag, datacenter id, and node id. those logs are part of the audit package and can be exported to your SIEM. traces show each hop.
[09:41] [00:09:41] Lars: ok, about support access — do you have time-bounded support access logs? we need to see who accessed what and when.
[09:49] Alex: yes support access is logged with reason codes, approver, and duration. we support JIT access and will send access logs as part of quarterly audits.
[10:06] Erik: if we run a POC, can we have an EU-only endpoint for the pilot and a test dataset?
[10:13] Alex: yes that's our recommended POC. we can spin up an EU-only hosted endpoint or a small Dedicated pool, depending on throughput needs.
[10:22] Maja: estimate the timeline — how long to stand up EU-only hosted pinning config vs dedicated?
[10:29] Priya: EU-only hosted pinning config is quick — config change + policy enforcement, we can do within a week. Dedicated reserved capacity depends on GPU availability but usually 2-4 weeks for initial capacity. Private on-prem is longer.
[10:45] [00:10:45] Sofia: what about data erasure? we need proof of deletion for regulatory requests.
[10:52] Priya: we have data deletion APIs and can provide deletion proofs: deletion logs, snapshot purge, and key rotation to render data unrecoverable. we'll provide the deletion flow docs.
[11:07] Lars: great. for legal we need DPA and examples of contract language referencing sub-processors and region pinning.
[11:15] Alex: will do.
[11:20] [00:11:20] Priya: small note: some transcription — (laughs) sorry — some of our internal product names sometimes transcribe wrong; the Console has per-route controls.
[11:34] Maja: competitor question — BigCloudAI says they do EU-only but their control plane still pings US. how do you compare?
[11:43] Alex: we explicitly provide an option for EU-only control plane via Dedicated/Private; for hosted this is an opt-in configuration and we will provide architecture proofs and logs. we position ourselves as production-first so you get the operational artifacts auditors look for.
[12:01] [00:12:01] Erik: any penalties or SLA credits if a cross-border processing incident occurs?
[12:08] Alex: we'll include standard SLA language and incident handling in the contract; cross-border incidents are treated as data incidents and handled per DPA. specifics can be negotiated.
[12:20] Priya: want to show quick example of API payload for residency... (screen share description)
[12:28] Priya: "{ \"region_pin\": \"eu-central-1\", \"residency_policy\": \"strict\" }"  - that sets strict residency and disables cross-region fallbacks.
[12:44] Sofia: nice. can you also provide IP ranges so our firewall team can whitelist?
[12:51] Alex: yes we'll include IP ranges per region and the CIDR blocks used by our agents.
[12:58] [00:12:58] Maja: one more on sub-processors — if a sub-processor changes, can we require 30-day notice and the ability to terminate?
[13:07] Eric (Legal - mislabelled Erik earlier): contractually termination clauses are something we'll review — we'll provide sample language, typically with notice and cure periods; for critical sub-processors we can add additional protections.
[13:27] Lars: i think we've covered the core. let's recap next steps.
[13:33] Alex: recap — Redwood will: 1) send SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation, pen test summary, and sub-processor list; 2) Priya will send EU-only architecture diagram and residency config examples; 3) Redwood Ops will stand up EU-only pilot endpoint for POC; 4) Redwood legal to share DPA with SCCs and proposed subcontractor notice terms.
[13:58] Maja: timeline — we'd like SOC docs asap and pilot next week if possible.
[14:04] Alex: we'll send docs by 2026-11-07, diagrams by 11-10, and aim to start pilot week of 11-16.
[14:12] [00:14:12] Erik: thanks, and please include contact for escalation.
[14:18] Alex: will include escalation contacts. thanks everyone.
[14:23] [00:14:23] -- meeting end --

Notes: transcript contains minor mis-transcriptions (names, acronyms), occasional run-on sentences and filler. References: SOC2 pack link (sent later), DPA template (link), architecture diag (link).
